correctness.rationale: For arbitrary odd prime and m,n>=2 the Laplacian identity (a+b)I-J_m tensor I-I tensor J_n is exact. In the nonzero cases tensor eigenspaces yield all nonzero and zero-primary blocks. In the one-divisible case nilpotent J_m has a single size-two Jordan block and the other eigenvalue block generates the p-factor in period counts. When both dimensions are divisible by p, L^2=2 J_m tensor J_n has rank one and L^3=0, while a row/column-sum surjectivity argument proves rank L=m+n-2; these steps establish the sharp size-three Jordan block and the 1-1/p maximum-depth fraction. General nilpotent/invertible decomposition and Möbius inversion give the exact independent depth-period census. The reproducible verifier corroborates 147 matrix-rank instances, 136 iterate-fixed-space instances, and 30,080 exhaustively simulated states, without using finite tests as a substitute for the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The complete odd-prime graph-Laplacian recurrence census is not a restatement of the published rectangular/square rook Smith forms, general finite-field dynamical methods, binary Cartesian-product parity theorems, or lattice prime-power kernel dilation. Peeters (2002), Theorem 3.4, covers power ranks of the square divisible-dimension Hamming subcase, and hence that special extinction bound is prior-covered. The full classification on unequal rectangular dimensions, the mixed-residue Jordan periods and joint depth-period census are not supplied or implied by those cited sources without additional structural work. Full text of the two most relevant primary arXiv sources and the published Laurent-polynomial result was compared. Unindexed historical equivalence remains possible.
residual_risks: Earlier rectangular rook-graph integral Smith and critical-group papers were identified through arXiv:1507.06583v1 but not all independently read in full; an unpublished odd-prime similarity census could be elsewhere.
General finite-field linear automaton methods can calculate each case and may conceal an equivalent parameter specialization in another source; a semantic search alone does not prove absence.

value.rationale: The complete attractor/transient phase diagram for finite graph heat-like modular dynamics is an independently natural question because the integer graph Laplacian is singular but modular iterations may exhibit nonzero cycles. The all-size three-step extinction phenomenon and dimension-independent exact fraction 1-1/p are structural boundaries not accessible from a single stationary kernel dimension or integer Smith form. The result supplies exact primitive periods and whole-basin shape for every rectangular rook graph and odd prime, beyond a narrow arbitrary numerical invariant; generalizations to other graph product classes are mathematically motivated but not claimed. The known square p-rank subcase is acknowledged; the value claim rests on the genuinely two-independent-size, mixed-residue complete dynamical phase diagram and cross-parameter exact counting.
